parole.significato: Derives nouns indicating a group or community
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kunta, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kunta. Cognate to Finnish kunta.

parole.significato: a barn, granary, warehouse, storehouse (building for storing food and other supplies, in a farm household)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Finnic *aitta (“storehouse”), probably from *ajadak (“to go (in a vehicle); to drive”) (with the suffix *-tta), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *aja- (“to drive; to hunt, chase”), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Háȷ́ati (“to drive, lead”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éǵeti (“to be driv
From Proto-Finnic *arvo, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *arwa (“price, value”), of Indo-Iranic origin. Cognate to Finnish arvo.

From Proto-Finnic *asën, possibly already Proto-Finno-Ugric *ëśema – ultimately from Proto-Uralic *ëśe-. Cognates include Finnish asema (“station, location”), Erzya эзем (ezem, “place, bench”) and possibly Northern Khanty ӑсәм (ăsəm, “pillow”) and Northern Mansi осма (osma, “pillow”), as well as Est

parole.significato: to open (to move something from a closed, enclosed state to an open state)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *avait'ak, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *aŋa-. Cognate with Finnish avata.
From Proto-Finnic *hap'oin, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *čappa. Cognates include Finnish hapan and Hungarian savanyú.

From Proto-Finnic *hiiri, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *šiŋere. Cognates include Finnish hiiri, Erzya чеерь (čejeŕ), Northern Mansi таӈкер (taňker), Hungarian egér. The computing sense is a semantic loan from English mouse.

Probably from Proto-Finnic *ääni, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *äne. Cognates include Votic ääli, Livonian ēļ; Finnish and Ingrian ääni, Karelian and Livvi iäni, Veps änʹ; Northern Sami jietna (“sound”) and Hungarian ének (“song”). Note that, if this etymology were to be correct, an unclear secondary chan
From Proto-Finnic *igen, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ikene. Cognate with Finnish ien and Hungarian íny.
From Proto-Finnic *jalka, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *jalka. Cognates include Finnish jalka, Ter Sami jillˈke, and Hungarian gyalog.
From Proto-Finnic *jäsen, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *jäsne, *jäse, or *jäsi (“joint”). Cognate with Finnish jäsen and Hungarian íz.

From Proto-Finnic *jää, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *jäŋe. Cognates include Finnish jää, Komi-Permyak йи (ji), Udmurt йӧ (jö), Northern Sami jiekŋa, Hungarian jég, Northern Mansi я̄ӈк (â̄ňk) and Eastern Khanty йӛӈк (jjəṇk).
From Proto-Finnic *kakci, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kakta. The final vowel was modified by analogy with *ükci (“one”).

From Proto-Finnic *keedäk, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *keje-. Cognate to Finnish kiehua, Votic čihhua, Eastern Mari кӱаш (küaš, “to boil, to cook, to sunbathe”), Hungarian köved, köveszt, küeszt (“to boil”), and possibly Forest Enets [script needed] (kū-, “to ripen, to mature (for berries)”).

From Proto-Finnic *kehä, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *keččä. Cognates include Finnish kehä, Northern Sami giessat (“to wrap”), Erzya чи (či, “sun, day”), Moksha ши (ši, “sun, day”), Eastern Mari кече (keče, “sun, day”), Udmurt киш (kiš, “snare”), Komi-Zyrian киш (kiš, “ring, halo”), Eastern Khanty кӫтш (
From Proto-Finnic *kivi, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kiwe. Cognate with Finnish kivi, Hungarian kő.

parole.significato: entrance hallway (the room between the front door and rest of the building)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kota, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kota.

parole.significato: home (house or structure in which someone lives)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *koto, derived from Proto-Finnic *kota, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kota. Possibly a loan from Proto-Indo-European *koth₁o. Compare Persian کد (kad). Cognate to Finnish kota and koto, Hungarian ház. See also koda.
From Proto-Finnic *kolmi, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kolme. Cognates include Finnish kolme, Northern Khanty хәԯум (həłum), Northern Mansi хӯрум (hūrum) and Hungarian három.

parole.significato: blister (sudden onset of a small local swelling, a bump on the skin)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kupla (“bubble”), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kupla. Cognates include Finnish kupla (“bubble”), Ingrian kupla (“heap; crest”), Karelian kubla (“debris on the water”), Livvi kublu (“swamp”), Ludian kubl (“swim bladder”); Southern Sami gåbloe (“lung”), Inari Sami koble (“perch roe”), Sk
From Proto-Finnic *kulma, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kuľma (“corner of the eye”). Cognate to Finnish kulma, Veps kulm, and Northern Khanty ҳулӛм (ḥuljəm, “eyebrow”).
From Proto-Finnic *kuuci, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kutte, from which also Finnish kuusi and Hungarian hat.

From Proto-Finnic *kanto, probably from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kanta, the same root as kand (“heel”) (Proto-Finnic *kanta). Another theory suggests a borrowing from Proto-Indo-Iranian *skandʰás, compare Sanskrit स्कन्ध (skandha). The irregular change *a > ä has occurred to differentiate from kand (“heel
From Proto-Finnic *käci, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *käte. Cognate with Finnish käsi, Erzya кедь (keď) and Hungarian kéz.
From Proto-Finnic *küünärä, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *küńä. Related to Finnish kyynärä and Hungarian könyök.

parole.significato: steam or vapour created from water being thrown on a hot surface
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *leülü, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *lewle (“spirit, soul”).
From Proto-Finnic *lintu, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *lunta or *linta, compare with Finnish lintu, Ter Sami lonnˈt, Northern Mansi лунт (lunt) and Hungarian lúd.
From Proto-Finnic *meci, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *mete, which is probably borrowed from Proto-Indo-European *médʰu. Cognates include Hungarian méz.
From Proto-Finnic *muu, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *mu. Cognate with Finnish muu, Northern Mansi мо̄т (mōt), Hungarian más.

parole.significato: to commemorate, to remember with honour
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mäle-, possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric [Term?]. Cognate to Votic mälehtä (“to remember”), Komi-Zyrian малавны (malavny, “to feel, to fumble”), Eastern Khanty [Term?] (“to fumble”), and Northern Mansi ма̄лейи (māleji, “to fumble”).

From Proto-Finnic *muistadak, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *muja-. Cognate to Finnish muistaa, Veps muštta, Erzya муемс (mujems, “to find”), Eastern Mari муаш (muaš, “to find, to get, to understand, to decide”), Northern Khanty мўйәптә- (mŭjəptə-, “to let sb guess sth”), and possibly Komi-Zyrian мойд (moj
From Proto-Finnic *mët'os, possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric [Term?]. Cognate to Finnish mettos, Livonian mõtūks, and possibly Northern Mansi [script needed] (mansin).
From Proto-Finnic *möötä, derived from Proto-Finnic *möö-, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *müŋä (“rear, beyond”). Cognate with Finnish myötä.
From Proto-Finnic *neljä, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *neljä. Cognate with Finnish neljä and Hungarian négy.
From Proto-Finnic *noita, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *nojta.
From Proto-Finnic *osa, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ońća. Cognates include Finnish osa and Hungarian oszt.

parole.significato: horsefly, breezefly, gadfly, forest fly (fly of the family Tabanidae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *parma, originally onomatopoetic. Cognate to Finnish paarma, Ingrian paarma. Possibly already from Proto-Finno-Ugric *parma: compare Eastern Mari пормо (pormo) and Erzya промо (promo), пуромо (puromo).

parole.significato: a group of birds, fish, or insects; a flock, a swarm or a school
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *parvi, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *parwɜ or *parɜ-wɜ. Cognate with Finnish parvi and Northern Khanty пөр (pør, “flock, group; raft”).

From Proto-Finnic *parvi, from Proto-Finno-Ugric [Term?]. Possibly the same root as in parv (“flock”). Cognates include Finnish parvi (“balcony”), Northern Mansi [script needed] (pōra, “raft”), and Northern Selkup [script needed] (pōri̮, “barn, storage platform”).

From Proto-Finnic *pihlä, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pićlä. Cognates include Finnish pihlaja, Erzya пизёл (piźol), Eastern Mari пызле (pyzĺe), Udmurt палэзь (paleź), Komi-Zyrian пелысь (pelyś) and Northern Khanty писяр (pisjar).
From Proto-Finnic *pilvi, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pilwe. Cognate with Finnish pilvi and Hungarian felhő.
From Proto-Finnic *punka, further origin uncertain. Possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *poŋka (“tuber, boil, unevenness”), along with Hungarian bog.
From Proto-Finnic *perä, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *perä. Cognate to Finnish perä.

From Proto-Finnic *pöörtädäk, ultimately from Proto-Finno-Ugric *peŋärä. Compare with Hungarian forog (“to revolve, to rotate”), Finnish pyörtää (“to turn around, return”), pyöriä (“to rotate”), pyöreä (“round”), and Ter Sami jorbɨsˈ (“round”).

From Proto-Finnic *repäinen, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *repä, likely a loan from Proto-Indo-Iranian *reupōśo-. Compare Persian روباه (rubâh, “fox”) and Avestan 𐬎𐬭𐬎𐬞𐬌 (urupi, “certain breed of dog”). Cognate of Finnish repo and Veps reboi. See also rebu.

From Proto-Finnic *sata, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śëta (“hundred”). Cognates include Finnish sata, Northern Mansi са̄т (sāt, “hundred”) and Hungarian száz. Originally borrowed from an Indo-Iranian language; compare Avestan 𐬯𐬀𐬙𐬀 (sata), Sanskrit शत (śatá).
From Proto-Finnic *sappi, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *säppä. Cognates include Finnish sappi, Hungarian epe.
From Proto-Finnic *sarvi (compare Finnish sarvi), from the same Proto-Finno-Ugric root *śarwe as Hungarian szarv.
From Proto-Finnic *sauvi, possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śawe ~ *śawwe.
From Proto-Finnic *siili, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śijele.
From Proto-Finnic *suladak, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *sula-. By surface analysis, sula + -ma.
From Proto-Finnic *surdak, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śure-.
From Proto-Finnic *säkä, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śäkä. Cognate with Northern Mansi [script needed] (siɣ, “burbot”).

parole.significato: to drive (a vehicle); to ride (a bicycle, a horse, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *soittadak (“to play (a musical instrument); to move fast; to scold”), ultimately from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śoje (“to ring, to sound ?”). Cognates include Finnish soida (“to sound”), soittaa (“to play an instrument”), Livonian sõitõ (“to punish”), Votic sõitta (“to scold”), Ingrian s
From Proto-Finnic *solmi, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ćolme. Cognate to Finnish solmu, Votic sõlmi and sõlmu, Livvi solmi, Moksha [script needed] (śulma), and Hungarian csomó.

From Proto-Finnic *tarja, compare Karelian tarja (“chip, lath”). Possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric [Term?], compare Eastern Mari тер (ter, “sledge”) and Eastern Khanty тӓрәс (tärəs, “the bottom of a type of sledge made from laths”).

parole.significato: work (an activity requiring a person's mental or physical effort)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *töö, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *tewe.
From Proto-Finnic *tüvi, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *tüŋe. Cognates include Finnish tyvi, Hungarian tő.
From Proto-Finnic *tüüni, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *tiwä-ni. Originally only seen in the North-eastern and Saaremaa dialects, but brought into the standard language partially from Finnish.

From Proto-Finnic *valkëda, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wëlketa, from *walke or *wïlki (“light”). Cognate with Finnish valkea, Livonian vālda, Votic valka, Ingrian valkia, Karelian valgie, Livvi valgei, Ludian valged, Veps vauged, Northern Sami vielgat (from Proto-Samic *vielkëtē) and Eastern Mari волгы

From Proto-Finnic *vetädäk, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wetä, most likely a borrowing from Proto-Indo-European *wedʰ-. Cognate to Finnish vetää, Ludian vedädä, Erzya ветямс (veťams, “to carry, to lead”), and Hungarian vezet.
From Proto-Finnic *veri, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *were. Cognates include Hungarian vér and Finnish veri.

From Proto-Finnic *viimäinen. Cognate to Finnish viimeinen and Votic viimin. Probably derived from the same root as in viibima. Possibly ultimately from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wiŋe; compare Hungarian vég.
Inherited from Proto-Finnic *väki, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wäke.
From Proto-Finnic *voi, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *waje. Cognates include Finnish voi, Hungarian vaj.

From Proto-Finnic *öö, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *üje. Cognates include Ingrian öö, Ludian üö, Finnish yö, Karelian yö, Livonian īe, Northern Sami idja, Inari Sami ijjâ, Erzya ве (ve), Udmurt уй (uj), Komi-Permyak ой (oj), Komi-Zyrian вой (voj), Southern Mansi йӣ (jī) and Hungarian éj.

From Proto-Finnic *üdin, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wideme. Cognate with Finnish ydin (“core, kernel; marrow”), Karelian yjin, Livvi üdin, Northern Sami ađa (“(bone with) marrow”) (from Proto-Samic *ëδëm), Erzya удем (udem, “brain, intellect; marrow”), Eastern Mari вем (vem, “brain; marrow”), Udmurt ви
From Proto-Finnic *ükci, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ükte. Cognates include Finnish yksi.
